doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Setting fees and exclusive commissions
summary: He has a standard fee, negotiates, and prices exclusives differently.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And how do you decide on what to charge?

I have a kind of a standard fee and then I tell the group look — especially if it’s a group that’s a professional or a highly touted university group, if it’s something that I really don’t have a lot of limitations to then I’ll work with you. If you can’t afford my price, let © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

me know what you can afford and maybe we can meet in the middle or something like that. Or if you wouldn’t mind — you know some places ask you to write them a chart and then tell me it’s got to be an exclusive, like I can’t play it with my group, I can’t have it published, like they want an exclusive for their group because they’re paying all this money. And I understand completely. So with that I set my price a little differently and things like that.
